  # placeholder: true # dashed "Video goes here" box when neither is set
  # poster: "assets/intro_poster.png"
  autoplay: true
  muted: true
  loop: true
  no-controls: true # no player controls/hover overlay, no click-to-pause; YouTube shows its thumbnail for ~3.5s to hide its start-up overlay
title-audio:

  loop: false

  image: "assets/hsma_logo.png"
  alt: "HSMA logo"
  bare: true # no shadow box behind the transparent logo
format:
  live-revealjs:
    pagetitle: "HSMA Session"
    output-file: index.html # ensures picked up by github hosting
# The output *directory* (docs/) is passed on the command line
# (`quarto render --output-dir docs`, see README.md) -- not set here, and
# not in _quarto.yml either. A per-document output-dir key looks like it
# would let each deck publish to its own folder, but for this project type
# Quarto ignores it silently. Setting it at the project level instead works
# for rendering, but breaks `quarto preview` of a single ad-hoc file (see
# _quarto.yml's comment). If you add a second deck, give it its own
# _quarto-<name>.yml project profile (render + docs-keep, no output-dir) and
# always render it with `quarto render --profile <name> --output-dir
# docs_<name>` -- see the HSMA vidigi animations deck repo for a worked
# example with two decks.
# Shared format/execute/filters/plugins config (including theme,
# template-partials and title-slide-attributes) lives in _metadata.yml --
# Quarto merges it in automatically for every document in the project,
# including sections rendered/previewed standalone. Keeping it out of here
# avoids two copies of that config drifting apart.

## Defining code snippets in the qmd file

```{python}
import plotly.express as px

px.scatter(x=[1,2,3], y=[2,3,4])
```


## Defining and running code snippets in the qmd file

```{python}
#| eval: true

import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio
pio.renderers.default = "notebook"

px.scatter(x=[1,2,3], y=[2,3,4], height=400)
```

## Including just the output

```{python}
#| eval: true
#| echo: false

import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio
pio.renderers.default = "notebook"

px.scatter(x=[1,2,3], y=[2,3,4])
```

## Embedded Streamlit

```{stlite-python}
import micropip
await micropip.install("plotly")

import streamlit as st
from plotly import express as px

st.title("Sample App")

st.slider("Choose a number between 1 and 10", min_value=1, max_value=10, value=5)

st.plotly_chart(
    px.scatter(x=[1,2,3], y=[2,3,4])
)
```

## Fade-in-then-out-lists

You can use the {.focus-list} div to auto fade in and out as you move through a list

::: {.focus-list}
* First important point
* Second important point (previous one dims!)
* Third important point
:::


## Fade-in-then-out-lists

This works with indented lists too

::: {.focus-list}
* First important point
  * And a sub-point on that matter
* Second important point (previous one dims!)
  * And a sub-point on that matter
    * ... and a really nested point
* Third important point
:::




## Code focus

Using reunings code focus extension, we can highlight different parts of a code example.

```{python}
#| eval: false
answer = "42"
question = "What is the answer to life, the universe, and everything?"
print(f"Question: '{question}'\n Answer: '{answer}'")
```

::: {.fragment .current-only data-code-focus="1"}
When this fragment is shown, the first line of code will have the `focus` class added to it and it gets highlighted.
:::

::: {.fragment .current-only data-code-focus="3"}
Then this line when we move through
:::

## Custom title slide layout

The title slide (the very first slide of the deck) is generated from the
`title-slide.html` partial and styled by `title-slide.scss`. It is driven
entirely by YAML frontmatter keys — see the top of this file for the values
used to build this deck's title slide:

- `title`, `subtitle` — the module/session text
- `author` — as before; the author name is coloured via `$hsma-title-author-color`
- `tagline` — short strapline, coloured via `$hsma-title-tagline-color`
- `partner-logo` / `partner-logo-alt` — a logo shown on a white plate, top-right

## Custom title slide layout (continued)

- `title-image` — a small image/GIF (or `video:`) shown above the title text
- `title-media-a` — a single image/video panel, top-left of the slide (`bare: true` drops its shadow box)
- `title-media` — a list of image/video panels, bottom-right of the slide
- `title-video` — a video panel, bottom-right: `youtube:` (video ID) or `video:` (file); `no-controls: true` hides the player UI; `placeholder: true` shows an empty box

## Custom title slide layout (continued)

- `splash` — adds a slide *before* the title slide with just `logos` over the
  banner (optional `background:` overrides the title slide's background); each
  logo takes an optional `position:` (e.g. `top-centre`, `bottom-right`) and `height:`
- `title-audio` — `src:` (and optional `loop: true`) for audio that starts when
  the title slide is shown and stops when you move off it
- `partner-logo-plate` — `none` or `dark` for white logos that vanish on the white plate

Every key is optional. Leave all of them out and the title slide falls back
to the original centred title/author layout.

Each media slot accepts either `image:` (works for GIFs too) or `video:`
(plus optional `poster:` and `autoplay: true`).

## Custom Title Slide - Escape hatch

If a deck needs a hand-built title slide instead of the generated one, add
`data-visibility: hidden` to `title-slide-attributes` to hide the generated
slide, then reuse the same styling on a normal slide with the `.hsma-title`
class and the `.hsma-ts-*` slot classes shown below:

```markdown
::: {.hsma-title}

::: {.hsma-ts-text}
# My Custom Title
:::

:::
```
